A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same q-exponential policy study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Equations, experiments, and displays can be matched despite relocation, renumbering, and localized corruption of v3 hyperparameter cells.

before.justification: v2 reports original online classic-control experiments and offline D4RL MuJoCo comparisons, including learning curves and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds SAC hyperparameter-sweep results and sampling-time measurements.

M1.justification: The policy parameterizations, learned Student’s t degrees of freedom, actor objectives, q-Gaussian sampling procedure, and out-of-support action handling remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 introduce no procedural revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions use Mountain Car, Pendulum, and Acrobot, plus nine D4RL datasets spanning HalfCheetah, Hopper, and Walker2d at Medium, Medium-Expert, and Medium-Replay levels. The added analyses reuse these environments.

E2.justification: The evaluated policy distributions and actor-critic comparators remain the same. TD3BC already appears in v2’s appendix comparisons; v3’s new SAC sensitivity plot also uses existing policy comparators.

E3.justification: New Figure 11 evaluates SAC sweep outcomes using rewards averaged over the final 10% of training. Appendix D.3 adds a timing protocol drawing 100,000 samples from randomly initialized actors with HalfCheetah and Hopper dimensions. The retained benchmark training and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a limited sensitivity analysis across SAC hyperparameter sweeps on the three classic-control tasks (Figure 11), alongside a sampling-cost analysis. Existing policy-evolution and boundary-density analyses remain; the latter moves from the main text to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Figure 11 newly reports unequal sweep run counts across policy parameterizations and oversampling smaller sweeps with replacement. Existing seed-count disclosures and standard-error/interquartile-range reporting remain unchanged; the resampling does not establish additional independent runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds sweep-level outcomes and sampling times: sparse q-Gaussian, heavy-tailed q-Gaussian, and Gaussian respectively take 107.12, 72.09, and 27.94 seconds on HalfCheetah, and 98.13, 65.17, and 25.17 seconds on Hopper. Existing benchmark plots and boundary-density values are unchanged. Earlier per-agent and aggregate CPU-time estimates are removed.

T1.justification: Section 2 removes the restriction to a 'finite action space' from the MDP description, correcting the stated domain to accommodate the continuous-action study. Distribution definitions, mathematical derivations, and Appendix A–C equations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion extend the comparative performance/stability message to an explicit recommendation that Student’s t can serve as a 'drop-in replacement' for Gaussian policies. The broader q-exponential-family contribution and TAWAC performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 interprets similar hyperparameter-sweep behavior as suggesting Student’s t will work where Gaussian policies work. It also removes the warning that the proposed boundary projection becomes a difficult constrained optimization problem in higher dimensions. New text describes Figure 5’s 75% win frequency as '75% more likely,' an interpretation the unchanged figure does not establish.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, expands dataset descriptions, and documents the sampling-time experiment. It removes Appendix E’s per-agent and aggregate compute accounting. Several learning-rate and temperature cells in v3 Tables 6–7 acquire stray text such as 'actually i uploaded now'; these are documentation defects, not evidence of deliberate setting changes.

R1.justification: The introduction and references add Simsekli et al. (2019), Bedi et al. (2024), and Chakraborty et al. (2023), expanding the motivation concerning heavy tails, Lévy processes, and sparse rewards. The existing research-positioning table and overall novelty framing remain.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand the Gaussian-policy motivation and notation explanation, update the abstract and conclusion, and revise dataset descriptions and Appendix E prose. Author information and conference headers change, while the section hierarchy and most text remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 11 and relocates v2 Table 3 to Appendix E as Table 8. Existing figures retain their graphical content, with limited resizing and reflow. The author block changes, and malformed hyperparameter entries distort the spacing and sizing of Tables 6–7.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful sensitivity and sampling-cost evidence plus a code-access pointer, while retaining the core experimental results. However, it introduces corrupted hyperparameter entries, removes compute-budget accounting, and overinterprets Figure 5’s win frequency as '75% more likely.' These gains in supporting evidence and access coexist with regressions in reproducibility documentation and claim precision, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
